facts.text: Sedillo takes its name from the Sedillo family, who received a land grant there in 1819 and settled the area soon after.
The town sits within the historic Cañon de Carnué Land Grant, established in 1763 as a buffer against Apache and Comanche raids.
San Isidro Church, built in 1941 to replace an older structure, hosts the annual San Isidro fiesta on May 15 with traditional celebrations.
At about 7,146 feet, Sedillo’s isolated setting offers sweeping views of the Sandia Mountains from homes nestled among hills.
Summer monsoon storms deliver roughly half of Sedillo’s 15–20 inches of annual rainfall, while winter snow averages 44 inches each year.
Today, Sedillo functions mainly as a bedroom community for Albuquerque, yet family farms and community events keep its agrarian heritage alive.
